Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming this land for 25 years, so I know what I'm doing here.

---

**My 14 mu this year**

I split my land like this: 5 mu of stevia (that's my main cash crop, it's what pays for the kids' school and the household things), 6 mu for wheat-maize double crop (that's my grain, we need flour for the family and the maize feeds the pigs or gets sold), and 3 mu of cotton on the piece of land in the back that doesn't drain well — cotton handles it better than grain.

**Stevia (5 mu)** — This is where my real income comes from. The buyer from the company comes around and contracts with us, so I know roughly what the price will be. I'll transplant the seedlings around early May after I buy them from the nursery — I don't grow my own seedlings, too much trouble. I put down more fertilizer on stevia than on wheat because the yield difference matters — maybe 20 kg N per mu split in two applications, plus a compound fertilizer at transplanting. My wife and daughter-in-law help with the cutting — you cut it once in July, then it comes back and you cut again in September. It's labor-heavy, but the price per kg is good. I'll water it 3 times from my well, maybe 4 if it's a dry summer.

**Wheat (6 mu)** — I planted this back in October and it's already up. Now I need to think about spring topdressing. Last year I did about 10 kg of urea per mu at green-up and the yield was alright, around 450 kg/mu. The extension guy said 15 kg N total per mu is enough but I usually do a little more because my land on the east side is a bit sandy. Before planting last fall I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (about 50 kg) per mu. I'll irrigate 3 times — once at green-up, once at jointing, once at filling if it doesn't rain.

**Maize (6 mu)** — This goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 15-20. The window is tight — maybe 5 days to clear the wheat straw, do a quick no-till or shallow till, and plant. I use the planter from my neighbor (pay him 20 yuan/mu). I buy hybrid seed from the agro-shop, the one everyone around here uses — Zhengdan or similar. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then topdress urea at jointing when the maize is about knee-high. If the summer rain is good I may not irrigate at all; if it's dry I'll pump once or twice.

**Cotton (3 mu)** — Cotton prices haven't been great the last few years but I keep a small piece because that back field isn't good for grain. I'll plant mid-April with plastic film mulch — that's what everyone does here. Less fertilizer than grain, maybe 12-13 kg N/mu, but more pesticide because of the bollworms. My daughter-in-law helps me pick in September-October, it takes many trips through the field. The yield will be maybe 270 kg lint per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Why I'm not changing much this year** — My two sons both work in the county town, so they send some money home but they can't help in the field much except at harvest. With just me and my wife (and my daughter-in-law some days), I can't take on more stevia even though it pays better. The labor is the bottleneck, not the land. I'm also keeping cash reserves because my wife's back has been bothering her and we may need to see the doctor.
